content.text: Installation
Hooks were introduced in React 16.8, so any project using them needs react and react-dom at 16.8.0 or later. There's no separate hooks package to install — they ship as part of core React.

For new projects, scaffold with Vite rather than Create React App (which is no longer actively maintained): `npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react`. If you're adding hooks to an older class-component codebase, upgrade react/react-dom first and run the app's test suite before touching any components, since some third-party libraries pinned to older React versions may break.

npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react
cd my-app
npm install
npm run dev

A typical hooks-based project structure separates presentational components from the custom hooks that hold logic, so components stay focused on rendering.

useReducer

useReducer is the right tool once a component's state has more than two or three fields that update together, or when the next state depends on the previous one in a non-trivial way. It's the same pattern as Redux, just scoped to one component (or shared via Context).
The reducer function must be pure — no side effects, no mutating the existing state object. Always return a new object from each case.

useMemo Pitfalls

The most common mistake is reaching for useMemo before profiling anything — it has its own overhead (comparing dependencies each render), so wrapping cheap calculations in it can make things slower, not faster.

The second mistake is an incomplete dependency array: if useMemo references a value that isn't listed, it will silently return a stale cached result instead of recomputing. Always let eslint-plugin-react-hooks fill in the array rather than typing it by hand.

Any effect that sets up a subscription, timer, or event listener must return a cleanup function, or the previous instance leaks every time the component re-renders or unmounts.

The gateway sits in front of five internal services and is the only component with a public IP. It terminates TLS, applies auth/rate-limiting, then proxies to the appropriate upstream over the internal network.
It's a stateless Node.js process behind a load balancer — no gateway instance holds session state, so any instance can be killed and restarted without draining connections manually.

content.text: Normalization
We standardize features to zero mean/unit variance (z-score) rather than min-max scaling, since several downstream models (logistic regression, SVM) assume roughly normal input distributions.

Constant-value columns have zero variance, which causes a divide-by-zero — the pipeline now guards this by skipping normalization for any column with variance below a small epsilon and logging a warning instead of crashing.

mean = X.mean(axis=0)
std = X.std(axis=0)
std[std < 1e-8] = 1.0  # guard against zero-variance columns
X_norm = (X - mean) / std

content.text: Installation
Hooks were introduced in React 16.8, so any project using them needs react and react-dom at 16.8.0 or later. There's no separate hooks package to install — they ship as part of core React.

For new projects, scaffold with Vite rather than Create React App (which is no longer actively maintained): `npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react`. If you're adding hooks to an older class-component codebase, upgrade react/react-dom first and run the app's test suite before touching any components, since some third-party libraries pinned to older React versions may break.

npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react
cd my-app
npm install
npm run dev

mergeRequests.title: Note edge case for zero-variance features
mergeRequests.description: Normalization step can divide by zero for constant-value columns; documenting the guard.

content.text: Normalization
We standardize features to zero mean/unit variance (z-score) rather than min-max scaling, since several downstream models (logistic regression, SVM) assume roughly normal input distributions.

Constant-value columns have zero variance, which causes a divide-by-zero — the pipeline now guards this by skipping normalization for any column with variance below a small epsilon and logging a warning instead of crashing.

mean = X.mean(axis=0)
std = X.std(axis=0)
std[std < 1e-8] = 1.0  # guard against zero-variance columns
X_norm = (X - mean) / std

content.text: Pipelines

The CI pipeline runs lint -> unit tests -> build -> integration tests -> deploy, with each stage gated on the previous one passing. Total pipeline time is currently ~9 minutes; anything pushing it past 12 needs justification in the PR.
Lint (parallel across services, ~30s)
Unit tests (parallel, ~2 min)
Build container images (~3 min, cached layers)
Integration tests against ephemeral environment (~3 min)
Deploy (canary, see Canary Releases)
